text: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority to make a final decision, provided that it is not amended so that it varies with City Policy or by-laws. Transportation Services is reporting on the results of the traffic calming poll undertaken on Delisle Avenue, between Yonge Street and Deer Park Crescent. The poll provided a response rate of less than the 50 percent plus one ballot required by the traffic calming policy needed to confirm that there is a favourable consensus in the community to install speed humps on the subject section of Delisle Avenue. Accordingly, continuing the process to install speed humps on Delisle Avenue, between Yonge Street and Deer Park Crescent, is not recommended.

The Toronto and East York Community Council directed: 1. The installation of traffic calming (speed humps) on Delisle Avenue, between Yonge Street and Deer Park Crescent be authorized. 2. City Solicitor prepare a by-law to alter the roadway to install five speed humps on Delisle Avenue, between Yonge Street and Deer Park Crescent, generally as shown on Drawing No. 421G-2452, dated March 2017 attached to the report (April 2, 2019) from the Acting Director, Traffic Management, Transportation Services.
